content.text:
I submitted **index 12 (Al 0.39 / Sb 0.61)**. It had the highest EQE of the three compositions I measured: 0.00236%.

| Index | Al / Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | 0.11 / 0.89 | 0.00020 |
| 12 | 0.39 / 0.61 | **0.00236** |
| 10 | 0.51 / 0.49 | 0.00057 |

- **Budget:** I used all 3 merit measurements and 4 of the 5 XRD scans.
- **Structure:** XRD at indices 4, 8, 12 and 16 all show the same main pattern: a strong peak at Q≈2.786 Å⁻¹ and a second peak at 4.54 Å⁻¹ that gets weaker as Sb increases. So the line looks like a single phase, and the change in EQE comes from composition rather than a phase change. I didn't confirm which phase it is.
- **Where the true best probably is:** somewhere on the Sb-rich side of 1:1, likely around indices 11–14. With only three measurements, the true best could be a neighbour I didn't measure, such as 11, 13 or 14.
- **Al-rich end (indices 0–6):** I didn't measure it. EQE dropped from index 12 to index 10, so it most likely keeps falling as Al increases.

EQE is very low everywhere I measured (all well below 0.01%), so none of these compositions is a practical photoanode at 2.4 eV.
